detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, firelight and black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot opens on an insert on the red ring of sand at night: three separate puffs of thick green smoke going up one after another from behind the rim, each of them rolling and climbing at a normal walking pace, lit green from within, against a blue-black sky with the thin mast standing beside them; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is a hundred yards from the pit, low, a 135mm lens. The green smoke is lit from INSIDE. At the first frame the three puffs of green smoke climb up the CENTRE of the frame from the CENTRE to the TOP edge, each a sixth of the width of the frame. The dull red rim of the sand runs across the BOTTOM third from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, the thin mast stands at the RIGHT third, and a blue-black sky fills the rest. The shot is inside this place: the sand-pits on Horsell Common at night in 1894: the raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater lit red from inside by burning furze, the thin jointed mast standing above it with its polished mirror turning at the top, knee-deep heather and dark furze standing black to the horizon, young Scots pines black against a deep blue-black sky. The camera tilts up from the rim of the sand with small amplitude until all three puffs of green smoke are inside the picture, travelling a hand's breadth as the first puff climbs and spreads, the second goes up through it, the third follows, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 the mast stands unmoved beside them, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:05 the camera is tilting up through the last frame, and the action continues with it.

Cloth, boots, wood and glass carry the physical action, and the movement and low murmur of the people at work nearby carry under it throughout.
